title: Besicovitch's Theorem: ℚ-Linear Independence of √(squarefree)
problemStatement: Generalize OQ-01 (irrationality of √2+√3+√5) to Besicovitch's theorem: the square roots of distinct squarefree integers are linearly independent over ℚ; equivalently [ℚ(√p₁,…,√pₙ):ℚ]=2ⁿ for distinct primes, with the 2ⁿ subset products a ℚ-basis.

insights: OQ-01's 'square twice to isolate √30' is exactly the n=3 shadow of √2+√3+√5 being a primitive element of the degree-8 field ℚ(√2,√3,√5) (minpoly degree 8 > 1 ⟹ irrational)
The whole theorem reduces to ONE non-trivial step: √pₖ ∉ ℚ(√p₁,…,√pₖ₋₁) for a new prime pₖ (the induction heart). Upper bound ≤2ⁿ and the n=1 base case are Mathlib one-liners
Equivalent operational test of the heart (certified exactly): minpoly(Σ_{i≤k} √pᵢ) has exactly twice the degree of minpoly(Σ_{i<k} √pᵢ)
Independence of distinct squarefree √d follows from degree=2ⁿ because distinct squarefree d have distinct odd-power-prime signatures ⟹ distinct subset-product basis vectors
Sign-flip automorphism proof (σ_p: √p↦−√p) is the conceptual content of OQ-01's repeated squaring, but needs the same degree theorem to know the automorphisms exist — not strictly easier in Lean
mathlibGaps: No general multiquadratic degree-2ⁿ theorem in Mathlib v4.26.0
No non-membership lemma √pₖ ∉ ℚ(√p₁,…,√pₖ₋₁) — this is the ~250-450 LOC crux (BUILD-class, not blocked)
